start_here.headline: Start with timeline.
lines: START HERE: timeline.events is the cross-source entry point — one row per real-world event from every source, with timeline.search_text() / timeline.search_text_exact() over the whole corpus.
Then: marts_* for structured domain analysis (finance, contacts, messages, photos, inbox, receipts, calendar, ai_conversations).
Then: base_* for complete, faithful source detail — every timeline row names its source_table + source_pk so you can drill straight back to it.
derived_* holds the modelled facts in between (identity resolution, enrichment, transcripts, ledger history).

Enrichments are keyed per provider+model+prompt_version, so read them through marts_voice_memos.recordings unless you specifically want every attempt.

schemas.name: internal
schemas.comment: Implementation-only helper functions and types. Not a query surface.

schemas.name: marts_ai_conversations
schemas.comment: Stable AI-conversation read interface across every provider (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, pi, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT). Start with marts_ai_conversations.sessions for one row per session, then marts_ai_conversations.events for its turns.

schemas.name: marts_calendar
schemas.comment: Stable calendar read interface. Start with marts_calendar.events_with_voice_memos for meetings that have a recorded transcript; marts_calendar.unmatched_voice_memos holds the transcripts no calendar event claimed.

schemas.name: marts_contacts
schemas.comment: Stable contacts read interface across Apple and Google address books. Start with marts_contacts.contacts for one row per card; marts_contacts.contact_points gives the normalized emails/phones other sources join identities through.

schemas.name: marts_finance
schemas.comment: Stable finance read interface over the Plaid + manual-statement ledger. Start with marts_finance.net_worth (or .net_worth_history); marts_finance.security_transactions and .tax_lots answer holdings/cost-basis questions, and check marts_finance.position_coverage before quoting a return.

schemas.name: marts_inbox
schemas.comment: Stable inbox read interface: what is waiting for a reply. Start with marts_inbox.gmail_threads and marts_inbox.slack_items.

schemas.name: marts_messages
schemas.comment: Stable chat-message read interface. Start with marts_messages.messages, which conforms iMessage/SMS and WhatsApp into one column set; the per-source views marts_messages.apple_messages and marts_messages.whatsapp_messages keep each provider's full detail.

schemas.name: marts_ops
schemas.comment: Stable warehouse-operations read interface: which pipeline feeds each table, when it last delivered data, and whether it is healthy. Start with marts_ops.pipeline_health.

schemas.name: marts_photos
schemas.comment: Stable photos read interface. Start with marts_photos.photos, one row per deduplicated logical photo with its AI caption; marts_photos.files lists every underlying rendition across photo sources.

schemas.name: marts_receipts
schemas.comment: Stable receipts read interface. Start with marts_receipts.transaction_receipts, which links a receipt document to the finance transaction it settles.

schemas.name: marts_slack
schemas.comment: Stable Slack read interface. Start with marts_slack.image_fingerprints to identify an image by perceptual hash and resolve who uploaded it.

schemas.name: marts_voice_memos
schemas.comment: Stable voice-recording read interface across every voice source. Start with marts_voice_memos.recordings, one row per recording with its resolved title, summary and transcript; marts_voice_memos.transcript_segments holds the speaker-labelled utterances.

schemas.name: ops
schemas.comment: Implementation detail: sync cursors, watermarks and runtime state. Not a query surface.

schemas.name: private
schemas.comment: Credentials and session snapshots. Never granted to the read-only query role.

schemas.name: timeline
schemas.comment: One row per real-world event across every source, plus the search_text()/search_text_exact() interface. Drill through source_table/source_pk for full detail; it is the recommended entry point, not the only truth.

objects.name: cycles
objects.comment: START HERE for the private WHOOP source. One row per cycle (sleep-onset to next sleep-onset, so start_at is not midnight). The same cycles as base_whoop.cycles, at the app API's richer grain; the public table remains the timeline's source.

objects.name: recoveries
objects.comment: hrv_rmssd_seconds is the private API's own unit (SECONDS); hrv_rmssd_milli is the same measurement in the milliseconds base_whoop.recoveries uses. Joining the two sources on the wrong one is a 1000x error.

objects.name: sleep_events
objects.comment: The hypnogram: one row per sleep stage span (LIGHT/REM/SWS/DISTURBANCES), ordered by event_index within a sleep's activity_id.

objects.name: heart_rate_samples
objects.comment: Continuous heart rate at the metrics-service grain (step_seconds is 6, 60 or 600). ~525k rows/year; range-scan it by (account, sample_at), the primary key.

objects.name: workout_heart_rate_samples
objects.comment: 6-second heart rate scoped to one workout. Cross-workout time ranges use the (account, sample_at) index, not the activity-leading primary key.

objects.name: journal_entries
objects.comment: What Zach logged himself, one row per (day, question). The only private-API table with a timeline adapter.

objects.name: sports
objects.comment: WHOOP's sport catalog: resolves base_whoop_private.workouts.sport_id to a name.

objects.name: documents
objects.comment: Tier-2 BFF payloads (trends, stress, cardio details, sleep deep dive) kept as faithful raw_json only, keyed by (kind, doc_key). These are UI documents: WHOOP restyles them without notice, so a typed column over them goes quietly null.

objects.name: transcription_runs
objects.comment: One row per transcription attempt per recording, carrying the provider's full transcript text. The resolved per-recording view is marts_voice_memos.recordings.

objects.name: transcript_segments
objects.comment: One row per speaker-labelled utterance of a transcription run. Joined to its recording in marts_voice_memos.transcript_segments.

objects.name: enrichments
objects.comment: Agent enrichment attempts, one row per (account, recording_id, provider, model, prompt_version) — so a recording has SEVERAL rows and a query that does not de-duplicate double-counts. Read marts_voice_memos.recordings for the resolved latest completed enrichment per recording.

objects.name: huddles
objects.comment: One row per Slack huddle — who started it, when it started and ended, and every participant — parsed from the huddle_thread message Slack posts in the channel. METADATA ONLY: nothing said in a huddle is in PDW, so absence of a decision here is never evidence it was not made.

objects.name: image_fingerprints
objects.comment: Slack image files with their 256-bit perceptual hash and the uploading user, for 'who sent this image?' lookups by XOR distance. Coverage is not proof of absence: only fingerprinted files appear (see derived_slack.file_fingerprints.status).

objects.name: gmail_threads
objects.comment: One row per Gmail INBOX thread with its latest message preview and unread/important counts: what is still waiting for a reply.

objects.name: slack_items
objects.comment: Slack items that want attention — unread DMs, mentions, and participating threads — one row each with a priority rank.

objects.name: contacts
objects.comment: Start here for people. One row per live contact card across Apple and Google address books; marts_contacts.contact_points explodes the same cards into normalized emails/phones for identity joins.

objects.name: contact_points
objects.comment: One row per (card, email/phone), with normalized_value in the shape other sources match on: lowercased emails, digits-only phones with a leading country code.

objects.name: apple_messages
objects.comment: Every base_apple_messages.messages column plus the resolved sender (sender_address/sender_name from base_apple_messages.handles and marts_contacts.contact_points). Apple-only; for cross-source message questions use marts_messages.messages.

objects.name: whatsapp_messages
objects.comment: WhatsApp messages with the chat kind, chat name and sender name already resolved. WhatsApp-only; for cross-source message questions use marts_messages.messages.

objects.name: messages
objects.comment: Start here for chat messages. One row per message across iMessage/SMS (base_apple_messages) and WhatsApp (base_whatsapp), conformed onto one column set so no caller has to hand-roll the cross-source UNION. chat_kind is the conformed vocabulary (direct/group/status/...); source_message_kind keeps the provider's own token. is_from_me and is_deleted are bigint 0/1, this warehouse's boolean. EVERY timestamp here is NULL when absent: the base tables are NOT NULL and store 'never' as 1970-01-01 (83% of recent messages have a sentinel date_delivered), so the sentinel is translated once here and ORDER BY, MIN() and IS NULL mean what they say. Tombstoned rows are included — filter is_deleted = 0 for live messages only.

objects.name: events
objects.comment: One row per turn or tool call across every AI-conversation source. A tool call and its result are separate rows; JSON columns are text, so cast before ->>.

objects.name: sessions
objects.comment: Start here for past AI sessions. One row per session across all six providers, with title, first prompt, repo/branch, device, model and token totals. Drill into marts_ai_conversations.events for the turns.

objects.name: files
objects.comment: Every rendition from every photo source, with the logical photo it resolved to and the dedup audit (match_method/match_score).

objects.name: photos
objects.comment: Start here for photos. One row per deduplicated logical photo with its AI caption and rendition counts; marts_photos.files lists every underlying rendition.

objects.name: canonical_renditions
objects.comment: Exactly one enrichable still per logical photo (the 1280px thumbnail), shaped for the shared file-enrichment runner. Not a general photo listing — use marts_photos.photos.

objects.name: events_with_voice_memos
objects.comment: Calendar events matched to a recorded voice memo, with the enrichment's transcript and summary. The recording side comes from marts_voice_memos.recordings.

objects.name: unmatched_voice_memos
objects.comment: Voice-memo transcripts that no calendar event claimed, with calendar_match_issue saying why. The counterpart of marts_calendar.events_with_voice_memos.

objects.name: recordings
objects.comment: Start here for voice recordings. One row per recording across BOTH voice sources — base_apple_voice_memos.files and base_alice_voice_recordings.recordings — with the latest completed derived_voice_memos.enrichments row resolved into title/summary/transcript/participants/action items/calendar match. Columns a source cannot provide are NULL rather than guessed: Alice recordings are not transcribed or enriched here. Every timestamp is NULL when absent, translating the warehouse's NOT NULL 1970-01-01 epoch sentinel. is_deleted is bigint 0/1.

objects.name: transcript_segments
objects.comment: Speaker-labelled transcript utterances with their recording's title and a spoken_at wall-clock instant derived from the segment offset. Timestamps are NULL when the recording has no known date (the warehouse's 1970-01-01 sentinel), so spoken_at is NULL rather than an offset from 1970. Only apple_voice_memos produces transcript segments today; the source column is there so another voice source can join without changing callers.

objects.name: security_transactions
objects.comment: Every share movement across Plaid and manual statements, deduped. Use this rather than marts_finance.investment_transactions, whose Plaid history stops at 730 days.

objects.name: tax_lots
objects.comment: FIFO lots with acquisition date, basis, term and unrealized gain. Splits and wash sales are not modelled; basis_known = 0 means the real basis lives at the origin account.

objects.name: position_coverage
objects.comment: How much of each position actually has a reconstructed lot history. Read this before quoting a return: 'partial', 'lots_exceed_holding' and 'basis_mismatch' all mean the number below is not the whole story.

objects.name: investment_holdings
objects.comment: Plaid-only passthrough of base_plaid.investment_holdings + securities: current holdings for Plaid-linked brokerages, and nothing else. Manual statements also carry positions (derived_finance.document_extractions.positions_json), but those are dated statement snapshots with no resolved account or security id, so unioning them here would mix current state with history under one name. For cross-source holdings work use marts_finance.tax_lots + marts_finance.position_coverage.

objects.name: investment_transactions
objects.comment: Plaid-only passthrough of base_plaid.investment_transactions, and Plaid's lookback is a hard 730 days. For the full cross-source trade history — Plaid plus every statement the corpus holds — use marts_finance.security_transactions.

objects.name: liabilities
objects.comment: Plaid-only passthrough of base_plaid.liabilities: statement balances, minimum payments and due dates for Plaid-linked credit/loan accounts. Liabilities the servicer does not expose through Plaid (the mortgage) are absent here; their balances arrive from statements as derived_finance.observations rows and are counted in marts_finance.net_worth.

objects.name: net_worth
objects.comment: Start here for money. One row per logical account carrying its latest observation, signed by side; net worth is SUM(signed_value). marts_finance.net_worth_history is the forward-filled daily series.

objects.name: net_worth_history
objects.comment: Forward-filled daily assets/liabilities/net series built from derived_finance.observations. Plaid keeps no balance history — this is it.

objects.name: account_freshness
objects.comment: Per-account recency of the finance ledger: when each account last produced an observation or a transaction.

objects.name: pipeline_health
objects.comment: Start here for warehouse health: one row per pipeline with status computed at read time against its own expected interval. marts_ops.table_freshness is the per-table detail.

objects.name: table_freshness
objects.comment: Per-table freshness: when the pipeline last wrote, how old the newest real-world event is, and whether the probe could run at all (probe_status).

objects.name: timeline_adapter_health
objects.comment: Per-adapter timeline currency: is this kind of data actually reaching timeline.events? The single `timeline` row in marts_ops.pipeline_health is a max() over every adapter and hides a frozen one. Note last_run_at is only stamped when a batch returned rows, so an idle adapter looks stalled; compare watermark_ingest_ts against the source relation instead.

objects.name: mart_view_health
objects.comment: Health of the marts_* read interface itself. A view has no stamped column and no relpages, so it cannot be probed the way a table is: each view is judged instead on the freshness of the stalest relation it reads (inputs resolved from pg_depend, each judged against its own pipeline's SLA), on a bounded SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1, and on whether its definition hash changed. Companion to marts_ops.pipeline_health, which covers tables.

objects.name: collation_health
objects.comment: Collation drift and unique-index divergence. This database has NO recorded collation baseline (pg_database.datcollversion is NULL) while the live library does report a version, and ALTER DATABASE ... REFRESH COLLATION VERSION refuses to create one from NULL - so Postgres can never raise its own mismatch warning and this view is the only cover. Reports only collations an index actually depends on. The duplicate-key probe is corroboration and cannot see a mis-ordered index that has no duplicates; amcheck's bt_index_check is the rigorous tool for that.

objects.name: plaid_item_health
objects.comment: One row per linked Plaid Item, naming the institution and accounts that stop updating when it breaks. status = 'action_required' means re-run `pdw ingest plaid link` for that institution.

objects.name: slack_conversation_health
objects.comment: Slack sync health per conversation type (im/mpim/private_channel/public_channel). Judges the OLDEST conversation metadata stamp, because that is what a bounded discovery walk has to keep cycling; marts_ops.pipeline_health aggregates Slack as one pipeline and cannot see one type stall. Message ages are context only — mpim legitimately has zero-message days.

objects.name: transaction_receipts
objects.comment: Receipt documents linked to the finance transaction they settle, with the agent's confidence and evidence.

objects.name: events
objects.comment: START HERE. One row per real-world event from every source, newest-first browsable and searchable through timeline.search_text()/search_text_exact(). Each row's source_table + source_pk drill straight back to the authoritative record.
